newsitem.title: INDIA: India says develops multi-barrel rocket launcher.
newsitem.headline: India says develops multi-barrel rocket launcher.

text.p: India has successfully tested a multi-barrel rocket launcher forming part of an integrated missile programme, a Defence Ministry spokesman said on Sunday.
The spokesman said test-firing of the Pinaka system was carried out between January 21 and 24 at a test site at Balasore, a coastal town on the Bay of Bengal in the eastern state of Orissa.
The Pinaka Area Weapon System fires 12 rockets in less than a minute and can target enemy targets at a range of 40 km (25 miles), the spokesman said quoting from a ministry statement.
The statement said the multi-barrel system, which can attack moving tanks, infantry columns and other targets, would complement the Prithvi missile which can strike from a range of 40 to 300 kms.
Prithvi, a surface-to-surface missile, has successfully completed trials for a 150-km (90-mile) version. The longer version of the missile with a range of 250 km is currently undergoing tests.
Prithvi is capable of delivering warheads of 1,000 kg (2,200 lb) up to a distance of 200 km. Indian defence analysts say the missile is perceived as a deterrent against Pakistan.
India's missile development programme includes surface-to-surface, surface-to-air and anti-tank missiles of varying ranges.

The United States, fearing an arms race between India and Pakistan, has urged New Delhi to halt missile testing permanently. The two South Asian neighbours have fought three wars since independence from Britain in 1947.
India detonated a nuclear device in 1974 but says it has not built a nuclear bomb.
